issues.legal_issue: A first appellate court reversing a trial court must give a reasoned decision addressing the material issues, evidence, and the trial court’s reasons.
material_facts: The trial court dismissed a title-declaration suit after finding that the plaintiff had not produced documents proving title.
The High Court reversed the trial court and decreed the suit, relying on the plaintiff’s genealogical evidence, survey records, and rent receipts.
The High Court did not frame points for determination or discuss the defendants’ evidence, including the plaintiff’s testimony that the disputed land had been purchased by the deceased woman.
The High Court also did not address the appellants’ argument that the suit was barred for omitting consequential relief.
issues.conclusion: The High Court had not discharged its duty as the first appellate court. Its judgment was set aside and the appeal was remitted for fresh consideration, without any opinion on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XLI Rule 31 CPC, a first appellate judgment must state the points for determination, decisions, and reasons. Although omission to frame points does not by itself invalidate a judgment if reasons based on the evidence are recorded, the first appellate court must address all material issues and evidence. When reversing factual findings, it must engage with the trial court’s reasons and explain why they are wrong. The Court relied on Vinod Kumar v. Gangadhar (2015) 1 SCC 391, Santosh Hazari v. Purushottam Tiwari (2001) 3 SCC 179, Madhukar v. Sangram (2001) 4 SCC 756, H.K.N. Swami v. Irshad Basith (2005) 10 SCC 243, Jagannath v. Arulappa (2005) 12 SCC 303, and B.V. Nagesh v. H.V. Sreenivasa Murthy (2010) 13 SCC 530. The consequential-relief objection under the proviso to Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act was raised but was not decided on its merits.

rule.if: first_appeal_from_original_decree and trial_findings_reversed and (material_evidence_not_addressed or trial_reasoning_not_engaged_with)

predicates.first_appeal_from_original_decree: The proceeding is a first appeal from an original decree.
predicates.trial_findings_reversed: The first appellate court reverses findings made by the trial court.
predicates.material_evidence_not_addressed: The first appellate court does not address material evidence bearing on the issues in the appeal.
predicates.trial_reasoning_not_engaged_with: The first appellate court does not explain why the trial court’s reasons for its findings are erroneous.

issues.definition: When a first appeal reverses trial findings without addressing material evidence or engaging with the trial court’s reasoning, the appellate judgment is set aside and the appeal is remanded.

issues.legal_issue: Purchasers impleaded as parties to a first appeal must receive an opportunity to present evidence and submissions supporting their claim to an interest in the disputed property.
material_facts: The appellants had purchased portions of the disputed property from the defendant and were impleaded as parties in the first appeal.
After impleading them, the High Court gave them no opportunity to adduce evidence or make submissions.
The High Court rejected their claim on the basis that the defendant had no title, without examining their claim or allowing them to substantiate that they were bona fide purchasers.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should have afforded the impleaded appellants an opportunity to adduce additional oral and documentary evidence and make submissions. The matter was remitted for a fresh hearing with that opportunity.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XLI Rule 27 CPC, the first appellate court should afford impleaded parties an opportunity to adduce additional evidence where necessary to substantiate their claim. A trial-court order against the original defendant does not preclude newly impleaded purchasers from presenting their own case. The Court also referred to the appellants’ impleadment under Order I Rule 10 CPC.

predicates.first_appeal_from_original_decree: The proceeding is a first appeal from an original decree.
predicates.purchasers_impleaded_in_appeal: Purchasers of disputed property are made parties to the first appeal.
predicates.purchasers_denied_opportunity_to_present: The appellate court does not allow the impleaded purchasers to present evidence or make submissions concerning their claim.

issues.definition: When purchasers are impleaded in a first appeal but denied an opportunity to present evidence or submissions, they must be given that opportunity.
